title: the guest is the designated test machine on the expected boot, x86_64, with systemd
group rosetun and two distinct ordinary accounts exist, both in the group, neither an administrator
no Rosetun unit, helper process, installed files or nftables table rosetun exist
/usr/sbin/nft, curl with tftp, dig and cgroup v2 are present
without Rosetun the probe address answers HTTPS on the physical interface, UDP 53 leaves it, the guest's resolver answers, and the host node accepts TCP
the helper runs as the systemd unit in its own cgroup leaf and offers the kill switch
rosetun status says the kill switch is in place and stays if the service crashes, and names nothing as missing
the running sing-box is rosetun-engine with no other group, CapEff, CapPrm and CapAmb exactly 0x3400, no new privileges, in the engines' leaf; the helper's bounding set is exactly the unit's
the engines' folders are root's with group rosetun-engine, 0710 and 0750: the engine reads its configuration and writes nothing there, and an ordinary account does not get in
connected with the kill switch: HTTPS to the probe address bound to the physical interface is refused
connected with the kill switch: HTTPS to the probe address through the tunnel answers
Local network off: TCP to the host node bound to the physical interface is refused
a foreign nftables table accepting everything at an earlier priority does not open the direct path, and the stand removes only that table
sing-box killed with SIGKILL: the direct path stays refused on every probe until the session is Connected again
nft flush ruleset during a kill-switch session: within ten seconds the table is back, the direct path is refused, and the journal and rosetun status say the rules were put back
sing-box holds CapEff, CapPrm and CapAmb 0x3400 without a rule by program and 0x83404 (CAP_SYS_PTRACE and CAP_DAC_READ_SEARCH on top) with one
a Direct rule for curl: curl of another account goes out of the physical interface, the same binary under another name through the tunnel
Direct by default and a Through VPN rule for curl: curl of another account goes through the tunnel, the same binary under another name out of the physical interface
adding and removing a rule by program while connected restarts sing-box with the capabilities it needs; the direct path stays refused throughout
the journal shows process lookups that found a program; the note counts them and those that did not, for the report
a disconnect removes the table and the direct path answers again
Local network on: TCP to the host node bound to the physical interface connects, the probe address does not
the DNS lock without the kill switch: UDP 53 to the DNS probe address bound to the physical interface is refused locally, HTTPS to the probe address there answers
the DNS lock: dig with the guest's own resolver is answered through the tunnel
with the nft binary not trusted the DNS lock cannot go in: the session connects without a table, rosetun status names the missing lock and its reason, and UDP 53 leaves the physical interface
expected leak: with the DNS lock not in place and sing-box killed, UDP 53 leaves the physical interface while it restarts, and rosetun status names the missing lock before and after

with the kill switch and "Local network": after the neighbor cache is flushed the IPv6 router answers a ping on its link-local address, and a UDP datagram to 2001:db8::1 on the physical interface is refused locally (skipped without an IPv6 router)
with the kill switch and without "Local network": a TCP session a peer namespace opened to the guest's sshd before the connect still gets answers, and the guest cannot send to the peer
HTTPS the guest forwards for a peer namespace (veth, NAT) out of the physical interface answers without Rosetun, is dropped under the kill switch and answers again after the disconnect
the helper killed with SIGKILL: the table stays, the direct path stays refused, systemd restarts the helper and it reports the network held closed
rosetun open-network from the first account removes the table and the direct path answers
the helper killed with SIGKILL during a DNS-lock session: systemd restarts it, it removes the table and says so, the network is not held and UDP 53 leaves the physical interface
the helper killed five times in a row: the direct path stays refused every time, and after that a connect answers through the tunnel with rules naming the current cgroups
systemctl stop during a kill-switch session removes the table and the direct path answers
file replacement and repeated restart-for-upgrade keep zero packets on the physical interface, report the hold and allow reconnect
